entries.9c4b4cef890d8e02bfd7b7efb3894359b0c5956e: <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.1.22" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Matt.1.22" sID="gen96175" type="section"/> <div sID="gen96176" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22. </hi><hi type="italic">Now all this was done</hi> It is ignorant and childish trifling to argue, that the name <hi type="italic">Jesus</hi> is given to the Son of God, because he is called <hi type="italic">Immanuel</hi> For Matthew does not confine this assertion to the single fact of the name, but includes whatever is heavenly and divine in the conception of Christ; and that is the reason why he employs the general term <hi type="italic">all</hi> We must now see how appropriately the prediction of Isaiah is applied. It is a well-known and remarkable passage, (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.7.14">Isaiah 7:14</reference>,) but perverted by the Jews with their accustomed malice; though the hatred of Christ and of truth, which they thus discover, is as blind and foolish as it is wicked. To such a pitch of impudence have many of their Rabbins proceeded, as to explain it in reference to King Hezekiah, who was then about fifteen years of age. And what, I ask, must be their rage for lying, when, in order to prevent the admission of clear light, they invert the order of nature, and shut up a youth in his mother’s womb, that he may be born sixteen years old? But the enemies of Christ deserve that God should strike them with a spirit of giddiness and insensibility, should<div eID="gen96176" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96177" type="x-p"/>“pour out upon them a spirit of deep sleep and close their eyes,” <lb/> (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.29.10">Isaiah 29:10</reference>.)<div eID="gen96177" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96178" type="x-p"/>Others apply it to a creature of their own fancy, some unknown son of Ahaz, whose birth Isaiah predicted. But with what propriety was he called <hi type="italic">Immanuel, </hi>or the land subjected to his sway, who closed his life in a private station and without honor? for shortly afterwards the prophet tells us that this child, whoever he was, would be ruler of the land. Equally absurd is the notion that this passage relates to the prophet’s son. On this subject we may remark, that Christian writers have very strangely misapprehended the prediction contained in the next chapter, by applying it to Christ. The prophet there says, that, instructed by a vision, he “went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son,” and that the child whom she bore was named by Divine command, ”Maher-shalal-hash-baz,” “Making speed to the spoil, hasten the prey,” (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.8.3">Isaiah 8:3</reference>.) All that is there described is approaching war, accompanied by fearful desolation; which makes it very manifest that the subjects are totally different.<div eID="gen96178" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96179" type="x-p"/>Let us now, therefore, investigate the true meaning of this passage. The city of Jerusalem is besieged. Ahaz trembles, and is almost dead with terror. The prophet is sent to assure him that God will protect the city. But a simple promise is not sufficient to compose his agitated mind. The prophet is sent to him, saying,<div eID="gen96179" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96180" type="x-p"/>“Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God; <lb/> ask it either in the depth, or in the height above,” <lb/> (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.7.11">Isaiah 7:11</reference>.)<div eID="gen96180" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96181" type="x-p"/>That wicked hypocrite, concealing his unbelief, disdains to ask a sign. The prophet rebukes him sharply, and at length adds,<div eID="gen96181" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96182" type="x-p"/>“The Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel,” <lb/> (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.7.14">Isaiah 7:14</reference>.)<div eID="gen96182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96183" type="x-p"/>We expound this as relating to Christ in the following manner: “You, the whole posterity of David, as far as lies in your power, endeavor to nullify the grace which is promised to you;” (for the prophet expressly calls them, by way of disgrace, the <hi type="italic">house of David,</hi> <reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.7.13">Isaiah 7:13</reference>;) “but your base infidelity will never prevent the truth of God from proving to be victorious. God promises that the city will be preserved safe and unhurt from its enemies. If his word is not enough, he is ready to give you the confirmation of such a sign as you may demand. You reject both favors, and spurn them from you; but God will remain steady to his engagement. For the promised Redeemer will come, in whom God will show himself to be fully present to his people.”<div eID="gen96183" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96184" type="x-p"/>The Jews reply, that Isaiah would have been at variance with everything like reason or probability, if he had given to the men of that age a sign, which was not to be exhibited till after the lapse of nearly eight hundred years. And then they assume the airs of haughty triumph, <note n="103"> <div sID="gen96185" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Faisant grand cas de leur argument</foreign>;” — “setting great store by their argument.”<div eID="gen96185" type="x-p"/> </note> as if this objection of the Christians had originated in ignorance or thoughtlessness, and were now forgotten and buried. But the solution, I think, is easy; provided we keep in view that a covenant of adoption was given to the Jews, on which the other acts of the divine kindness depended. There was then a general promise, by which God adopted the children of Abraham as a nation, and on which were founded all the special promises. Again, the foundation of this covenant was the Messiah. Now we hold, that the reason for delivering the city was, that it was the sanctuary of God, and out of it the Redeemer would come. But for this, Jerusalem would a hundred times have perished.<div eID="gen96184" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96186" type="x-p"/>Let pious readers now consider, when the royal family had openly rejected the sign which God had offered to them, if it was not suitable that the prophet should pass all at once to the Messiah, and address them in this manner: “Though this age is unworthy of the deliverance of which God has given me a promise, yet God is mindful of his covenant, and will rescue this city from its enemies. While he grants no particular sign to testify his grace, this one sign ought to be deemed more than sufficient to meet your wishes. from the stock of David the Messiah will arise.” Yet it must be observed that, when the prophet reminds unbelievers of the general covenant, it is a sort of reproof, because they did not accept of a particular sign. I have now, I think, proved that, when the door was shut against every kind of miracle, the prophet made an appropriate transition to Christ, for the purpose of leading unbelievers to reflect, that the only cause of the deliverance was the covenant that had been made with their fathers. And by this remarkable example has God been pleased to testify to all ages, that he followed with uninterrupted kindness the children of Abraham, only because in Christ, and not through their own merits, he had made with them a gracious covenant.<div eID="gen96186" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96187" type="x-p"/>There is another piece of sophistry by which the Jews endeavor to parry our argument. Immediately after the words in question, the prophet adds:<div eID="gen96187" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96188" type="x-p"/>“Before the child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings,” <lb/> (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.7.16">Isaiah 7:16</reference>.)<div eID="gen96188" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96189" type="x-p"/>Hence they infer, that the promised birth of the child would be delayed for a very short time; otherwise, it would not agree with the rapidly approaching change of the kingdoms, which, the prophet announeed, would take place before that child should have passed half the period of infancy. I reply, when Isaiah has given a sign of the future Savior, and declared that a child will be born, who is the true <hi type="italic">Immanuel, </hi>or — to use Paul’s language —<hi type="italic"> God manifest in the flesh,</hi> (<reference osisRef="Bible:1Tim.3.16">1 Timothy 3:16</reference>,) he proceeds to speak, in general terms, of all the children of his own time. A strong proof of this readily presents itself; for, after having spoken of the general promise of God, he returns to the special promise, which he had been commissioned to declare. The former passage, which relates to a final and complete redemption, describes one particular child, to whom alone belongs the name of God; while the latter passage, which relates to a special benefit then close at hand, determines the time by the childhood of those who were recently born, or would be born shortly afterwards.<div eID="gen96189" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96190" type="x-p"/>Hitherto, if I mistake not, I have refuted, by strong and conclusive arguments, the calumnies of the Jews, by which they endeavor to prevent the glory of Christ from appearing, with resplendent luster, in this prediction. It now remains for us to refute their sophistical reasoning about the Hebrew word <foreign xml:lang="he">עלמה</foreign><hi type="italic">, virgin</hi> <note n="104"> <div sID="gen96191" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Le mot Hebrieu <hi type="italic">Alma, </hi>pour lequel l'Evangeliste a use du mot de Vierge</foreign>;” — “the Hebrew word <hi type="italic">Alma, </hi>for which the Evangelist has used the word Virgin.”<div eID="gen96191" type="x-p"/> </note> They wantonly persecute Matthew for proving that Christ was born of a virgin, <note n="105"> <div sID="gen96192" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Le blamant de ce qu'il pretend prouver Jesus Christ estre nay d'une Vierge</foreign>;” — “blaming him for offering to prove Jesus Christ to be born of a Virgin.”<div eID="gen96192" type="x-p"/> </note> while the Hebrew noun merely signifies <hi type="italic">a young woman; </hi>and ridicule us for being led astray by the wrong translation <note n="106"> <div sID="gen96193" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Abusez par un mot mal tourne</foreign>;” — “deceived by a word ill translated.”<div eID="gen96193" type="x-p"/> </note> of a word, to believe that he was born by the Holy Spirit, of whom the prophet asserts no more than that he would be the son of a young woman. And, first, they display an excessive eagerness for disputation, by laboring <note n="107"> <div sID="gen96194" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="la">Urgent</foreign>;” — “<foreign xml:lang="fr">ils veulent a toute force</foreign>;” — “they attempt with their whole strength.”<div eID="gen96194" type="x-p"/> </note> to prove that a word, which is uniformly applied in Scripture to <hi type="italic">virgins, </hi>denotes here a young woman who had known a man. The etymology too agrees with Matthew’s translation of the word: for it means <hi type="italic">hiding,</hi> <note n="108"> <div sID="gen96195" type="x-p"/> <foreign xml:lang="he">עלמה</foreign> is derived from <foreign xml:lang="he">עלם</foreign>, <hi type="italic">to hide,</hi>—<hi type="italic">a </hi>verb not found in Kal, but so frequently in Niphal, (<foreign xml:lang="he">נעלם</foreign>,) Hiphil, (<foreign xml:lang="he">העלים</foreign>,) Hithpahel, (<foreign xml:lang="he">התעלם</foreign>,) that its meaning is fully ascertained. — <hi type="italic">Ed.</hi><div eID="gen96195" type="x-p"/> </note> which expresses the modesty that becomes a virgin. <note n="109"> <div sID="gen96196" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Car il emporte Retraitte ou Cachette, qui est pour denoter ceste honte honeste qui doit estre es vierges</foreign>;” — “for it signifies Retreat or Concealment, which serves to denote that becoming shame which ought to be in virgins.”<div eID="gen96196" type="x-p"/> </note> They produce a passage from the book of Proverbs, “the way of a man with a maids,” <foreign xml:lang="he">בעלמה</foreign>, (<reference osisRef="Bible:Prov.30.19">Proverbs 30:19</reference>.) But it does not at all support their views. Solomon speaks there of a young woman who has obtained the affections of a young man: but it does not follow as a matter of course, that the young man has seduced the object of his regard; or rather, the probability leans much more strongly to the other side. <note n="110"> <div sID="gen96197" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">C'est bien autrement: car il y a plus d'apparence au contraire</foreign>;”— “it is quite otherwise: for there is more probability on the opposite side.<div eID="gen96197" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen96190" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96198" type="x-p"/>But granting all that they ask as to the meaning of the word, the subject demonstrates, and compels the acknowledgment, that the prophet is speaking of a miraculous and extraordinary birth. He exclaims that he is bringing a sign from the Lord, and not an ordinary sign, but one superior to every other.<div eID="gen96198" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96199" type="x-p"/>The Lord himself shall give you a sign. <lb/> Behold, a virgin shall conceive, <lb/> (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.7.14">Isaiah 7:14</reference>.)<div eID="gen96199" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96200" type="x-p"/>If he were only to say, that a woman would bear a child, how ridiculous would that magnificent preface have been? Thus we see, that the insolence of the Jews exposes not only themselves, but the sacred mysteries of God, to scorn.<div eID="gen96200" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96201" type="x-p"/>Besides, a powerful argument may be drawn from the whole strain of the passage. <hi type="italic">Behold, a virgin shall conceive</hi> Why is no mention made of a man? It is because the prophet draws our attention to something very uncommon. Again, the virgin is commanded to name the child. <hi type="italic">Thou shalt call his name Immanuel</hi> In this respect, also, the prophet expresses something extraordinary: for, though it is frequently related in Scripture, that the names were given to children by their mothers, yet it was done by the authority of the fathers. When the prophet addresses his discourse to the virgin, he takes away from men, in respect to this child, that authority which is conferred upon them by the order of nature. Let this, therefore, be regarded as an established truth, that the prophet here refers to a remarkable miracle of God, and recommends it to the attentive and devout consideration of all the godly, — a miracle which is basely profaned by the Jews, who apply to the ordinary method of conception what is said in reference to the secret power of the Spirit.<div eID="gen96201" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.1.22" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen96175" osisID="Matt.1.22" type="section"/>
entries.b3a08b18bd15fcbec6935b184f9db1c81bca89fe: <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.1.23" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Matt.1.23" sID="gen96202" type="section"/> <div sID="gen96203" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23. </hi><hi type="italic">His name Immanuel</hi> The phrase, <hi type="italic">God is with us, </hi>is no doubt frequently employed in Scripture to denote, that he is present with us by his assistance and grace, and displays the power of his hand in our defense. But here we are instructed as to the <hi type="italic">manner</hi> in which God communicates with men. For out of Christ we are alienated from him; but through Christ we are not only received into his favor, but are made one with him. When Paul says, that the Jews under the law <hi type="italic">were nigh</hi> to God, (<reference osisRef="Bible:Eph.2.17">Ephesians 2:17</reference>,) and that a deadly <hi type="italic">enmity</hi> (<reference osisRef="Bible:Eph.2.15">Ephesians 2:15</reference>) subsisted between him and the Gentiles, he means only that, by shadows and figures, God then gave to the people whom he had adopted the tokens of his presence. That promise was still in force, “The Lord thy God is among you,” (<reference osisRef="Bible:Deut.7.21">Deuteronomy 7:21</reference>,) and, “This is my rest for ever,” (<reference osisRef="Bible:Ps.132.14">Psalm 132:14</reference>.) But while the familiar intercourse between God and the people depended on a Mediator, what had not yet fully taken place was shadowed out by symbols. His seat and residence is placed “between the Cherubim,” (<reference osisRef="Bible:Ps.80.1">Psalm 80:1</reference>,) because the ark was the figure and visible pledge of his glory.<div eID="gen96203" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96204" type="x-p"/>But in Christ the actual presence of God with his people, and not, as before, his shadowy presence, has been exhibited. <note n="111"> <div sID="gen96205" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Mais quand Christ est apparu en sa personne, le peuple a eu une presence de Dieu veritable, et non pas ombratile comme paravant</foreign>.”— “But when Christ appeared in his person, the people had a real presence of God, and not shadowy, as before.”<div eID="gen96205" type="x-p"/> </note> This is the reason, why Paul says, that “in him dwelleth all the fullness of the Godhead bodily,” (<reference osisRef="Bible:Col.2.9">Colossians 2:9</reference>.) And certainly he would not be a properly qualified Mediator, if he did not unite both natures in his person, and thus bring men into an alliance with God. Nor is there any force in the objection, about which the Jews make a good deal of noise, that the name of God is frequently applied to those memorials, by which he testified that he was present with believers.<div eID="gen96204" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96206" type="x-p"/>For it cannot be denied, that this name, <hi type="italic">Immanuel, </hi>contains an implied contrast between the presence of God, as exhibited in Christ, with every other kind of presence, which was manifested to the ancient people before his coming. If the reason of this name began to be actually true, when Christ appeared in the flesh, it follows that it was not completely, but only in part, that God was formerly united with the Fathers.<div eID="gen96206" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96207" type="x-p"/>Hence arises another proof, that Christ is <hi type="italic">God manifested in the flesh,</hi> (<reference osisRef="Bible:1Tim.3.16">1 Timothy 3:16</reference>.) He discharged, indeed, the office of Mediator from the beginning of the world; but as this depended wholly on the latest revelation, he is justly called Immanuel at that time, when clothed, as it were, with a new character, he appears in public as a Priest, to atone for the sins of men by the sacrifice of his body, to reconcile them to the Father by the price of his blood, and, in a word, to fulfill every part of the salvation of men. <note n="112"> <div sID="gen96208" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Somme, pour faire et accomplir toutes choses requises au salut du genre humain</foreign>;” — “in a word, to do and accomplish all things requisite for the salvation of the human race.”<div eID="gen96208" type="x-p"/> </note> The first thing which we ought to consider in this name is the divine majesty of Christ, so as to yield to him the reverence which is due to the only and eternal God. But we must not, at the same time, forget the fruit which God intended that we should collect and receive from this name. For whenever we contemplate the one person of Christ as God-man, we ought to hold it for certain that, if we are united to Christ by faith, we possess God.<div eID="gen96207" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96209" type="x-p"/>In the words, <hi type="italic">they shall call, </hi>there is a change of the number. But this is not at all at variance with what I have already said. True, the prophet addresses the virgin alone, and therefore uses the second person, <hi type="italic">Thou shalt call</hi> But from the time that this name was published, all the godly have an equal right to make this confession, that God has given himself to us to be enjoyed in Christ. <note n="113"> <div sID="gen96210" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Il appartient a tous fideles d'advouer et confesser que Dieu s'est communique et baille a nous en Christ</foreign>;” — “it belongs to all believers to own and confess that God has communicated and made over himself to us in Christ.”<div eID="gen96210" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen96209" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.1.23" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen96202" osisID="Matt.1.23" type="section"/>
entries.42bb80e1f85acd0ce8ca63f8854d3871889329ca: <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.1.24" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Matt.1.24" sID="gen96211" type="section"/> <div sID="gen96212" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24. </hi><hi type="italic">Joseph, being raised from sleep</hi> The ready performance, which is here described, serves not less to attest the certainty of Joseph’s faith, than to commend his obedience. For, if every scruple had not been removed, and his conscience fully pacified, he would never have proceeded so cheerfully, on a sudden change of opinion, <hi type="italic">to take unto him his wife, </hi>whose society, he lately thought, would pollute him. <note n="114"> <div sID="gen96213" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Laquelle un peu auparavant il ne vouloit recevoir, et lui sembloit qu'il se fust pollue en conversant avec elle</foreign>;” — “whom a little before he refused to receive, and seemed to him that he would be polluted by conversing with her.”<div eID="gen96213" type="x-p"/> </note> The dream must have carried some mark of Divinity, which did not allow his mind to hesitate. Next followed the effect of faith. Having learned the will of God, he instantly prepared himself to obey.<div eID="gen96212" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.1.24" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen96211" osisID="Matt.1.24" type="section"/>
entries.76070896dbd9a7d6d6ac03f9debe536557bc2ef6:
25. And knew her not This passage afforded the pretext for great disturbances, which were introduced into the Church, at a former period, by Helvidius. The inference he drew from it was, that Mary remained a virgin no longer than till her first birth, and that afterwards she had other children by her husband. Jerome, on the other hand, earnestly and copiously defended Mary’s perpetual virginity. Let us rest satisfied with this, that no just and well-grounded inference can be drawn from these words of the Evangelist, as to what took place after the birth of Christ. He is called first-born; but it is for the sole purpose of informing us that he was born of a virgin.
“Il est nomme Premier nay, mais non pour autre raison, sinon afin que nous sachions qu'il est nay d'une mere vierge, et qui jamais n'avoit eu enfant;” — “he is called First-born, but for no other reason than that we may know that he was born of a pure virgin, and who never had had a child.”
It is said that Joseph knew her not till she had brought forth her first-born son: but this is limited to that very time. What took place afterwards, the historian does not inform us. Such is well known to have been the practice of the inspired writers. Certainly, no man will ever raise a question on this subject, except from curiosity; and no man will obstinately keep up the argument, except from an extreme fondness for disputation.
LUKE 2:1-7
Luke 2:1-7
1. Now it happened in those days, an edict came out from Augustus Caesar, that the whole world should be registered.
“Mis par escrit;” — “put in writing.”
2. This first registration
“Ceste premiere description.”
was made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria. 3. And all went to make the return,
“Ut profiteretur.”
each in his own city. 4. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, into the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, (because he was of the house and lineage of David,) 5. To make the return with Mary
“Pour estre enroule avec Marie;” — “to be enrolled with Mary.”
his betrothed wife, who was pregnant. 6. And it happened while they were there, the days of bringing forth were fulfilled.
“Et comme ils estoyent la, advint que les jours d'icelle furent accom-. plis pour enfanter.” — “And as they were there, it happened that her days were accomplished for bringing forth.”
7. And she brought forth her first-born son, and wrapped him in bandages,
“Fasciis;” — “Bandelettes.”
and laid him in a manger;
“Une creiche.”
because there was no room for them in the inn.

               <ns0:head>CHAP. I.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1. THe Book of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 3.23.</ns0:note> the Generation of Jesus Christ, the Son of David, the Son of Abraham.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>The Book of the Generation,</ns0:hi> Signifieth no more than the <ns0:hi>writing</ns0:hi> containing the <ns0:hi>Genealogy</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Pedegree</ns0:hi>; for the Jews called all writings <ns0:hi>Books.</ns0:hi> Thus, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 32.10, 11. <ns0:hi>The Eviden<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces of a purchase</ns0:hi> is called the Book. So <ns0:hi>Isaiah,</ns0:hi> 50.1. and <ns0:hi>Mark.</ns0:hi> 10.4. the writings called a <ns0:hi>Bill of Divorce</ns0:hi> are both in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> called, a <ns0:hi>Book of Divorce.</ns0:hi> Thus in <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical Courts</ns0:hi> still, the term <ns0:hi>Libel</ns0:hi> (which signifieth a <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>tle Book</ns0:hi>) is used, so as these words, are not to be lookt upon as the <ns0:hi>Title</ns0:hi> to the whole Gospel according to St. <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew,</ns0:hi> b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t only to the following <ns0:hi>Pedegree</ns0:hi> of our <ns0:hi>Saviours Ancestors, of Iesus Christ,</ns0:hi> of that Person to whom the name of <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> was given by the <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> as we shall hear further, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20.21. <ns0:hi>Because he should save</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>People</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>their sins</ns0:hi> (for <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> as also <ns0:hi>Ioshuah</ns0:hi> signifies a <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Deliverer</ns0:hi>) and who also was the <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> prophesied of by <ns0:hi>Daniel, Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.25, 26. expected by the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> as doth ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pear from <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.41. (for <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> denoted the same Person, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 4, 25. only <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was an <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> word, and <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> extraction, both signifying <ns0:hi>Anointed,</ns0:hi> and so Gods designation of a Person to the Office of a <ns0:hi>Priest,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>King. The Christ</ns0:hi> signifyeth a designation to all three, <ns0:hi>The Son of David, the Son of Abraham</ns0:hi>: Not the immediate Son of either, but by a long Traduction, line<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally descended from both. <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> was long before <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid</ns0:hi> but is here put after him, either because he was a <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> or because, the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> expected <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> was to be the <ns0:hi>Son of David</ns0:hi>; Or because the <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> design was to begin the <ns0:hi>Pedegree</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> whom he therefore last mentioneth. Both are named, because both were concerned in the promise of Christ. It was made to <ns0:hi>Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 12.3. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 22.18. and to <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> renewed, and enlarged. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 89.36, 37. Hence it appeareth that the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> lookt that Christ should be the <ns0:hi>Son of David, Mat.</ns0:hi> 22.42. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 12.35<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Hence the Evangelist puts <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> in the front. From <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> derived themselves, they usually Gloryed, they had <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>their Father.</ns0:hi> The Evangelist by proving Christ, to have descended from <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Isaac,</ns0:hi> proveth him an <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> and to be descended from the <ns0:hi>seed</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>whom the Promise was made,</ns0:hi> and by proving him <ns0:hi>the Son of David,</ns0:hi> he proves him <ns0:hi>David's righteous Branch,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Branch</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>righteousness</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 23.5, 6. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 33.15. and so to have descended from the <ns0:hi>Royal Family.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2. Abraham begat Isaac, and Isaac begat Ja<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cob, and Jacob begat Judas and his Brethren.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Evangelist reckoneth the <ns0:hi>Genealogy</ns0:hi> of our Saviour, by three Periods; reckoning thrice fourteen Descents. The first <ns0:hi>Period</ns0:hi> began in <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> and ended in <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi> The second began in <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> and ended in <ns0:hi>Iehojachim.</ns0:hi> The third began with <ns0:hi>Iehojachim,</ns0:hi> and ended in <ns0:hi>Christ. Luke</ns0:hi> (as we shall see <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> its place) fetcheth our Saviours line, from <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> there is no difference betwixt. <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> they both reckoned up the same four<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teen Persons, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 3.32, 33, 34. But <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> repeating our Saviours Pedegree by his <ns0:hi>Mothers side,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> by his supposed Fathers side, <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> after <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> they must differ, <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> descending from <ns0:hi>Davids</ns0:hi> Family by his Son <ns0:hi>Nathan, Ioseph</ns0:hi> descending from him by <ns0:hi>Solomon.</ns0:hi> All <ns0:hi>Interpreters</ns0:hi> agree that there are great Difficulties, about the <ns0:hi>Genealogy</ns0:hi> of Christ, (especially in reconciling <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke.</ns0:hi>) And the Enemies of Christianity have in all times, made their advantage of them, to weaken our Faith as to the Gospel, but Christians ought to consider, 1. <ns0:hi>That the Iews had without doubt perfect Genealogies</ns0:hi>; and were more especi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally exact in keeping them as to the Royal Tribe of <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid,</ns0:hi> which was <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Priestly Tribe</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> that they might have a right <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> and it cannot be expected that after seventeen hundred years al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />most, we should make out <ns0:hi>Genealogies</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> as they could. 2. <ns0:hi>That they were very apt to make Strifes, about words, and endless Genealogies.</ns0:hi> As appears by the Apostles caution<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing both <ns0:hi>Timot<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> against it, <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.4. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 6.4. <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> 3.9. 3. <ns0:hi>That it had been a sufficient exception against Christ if they could have proved he had not line<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally descended from David.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>That tho they c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>villed at Christ for many things,</ns0:hi> yet, <ns0:hi>they never made any such Cavil.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>That we are forbidden S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ife, and endless Labour a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout Genealogy.</ns0:hi> And therefore it is the most unreasonable thing imaginable for us, to make such little Dissatisfactions, Grounds for us to question, or disbelieve the <ns0:hi>Gospel,</ns0:hi> because we cannot unty every knot we meet with in a Pedegree, but in this first <ns0:hi>Period,</ns0:hi> no such Difficulties occur. Both the <ns0:hi>Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelists</ns0:hi> are agreed, and the Old <ns0:hi>Testam<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nt</ns0:hi> agrees both: That <ns0:hi>Abraham begat Isaac</ns0:hi> (when he was an hundred years old) we are assured by <ns0:hi>Moses, Gen.</ns0:hi> 21.2.5. that <ns0:hi>Isaac begat Iacob,</ns0:hi> he also telleth us, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 25.26. So also that <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Brethren, Gen.</ns0:hi> 29.35. <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>Iacob's</ns0:hi> third Son by <ns0:hi>Leah,</ns0:hi> and that Son of whom dying <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> prophesied, That <ns0:hi>him should</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Brethren praise, and to him should his Fathers Children bow down. That the Scepter should not depart from Iudah, nor the Law<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />giver from between his Feet, until Shiloh came, and unto him should the gathering of the People be, Gen.</ns0:hi> 49.8, 9, 10. Tho <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> who was the first King of <ns0:hi>Israel (given them in wrath</ns0:hi>) was of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Benjamin,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 9.21. yet <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was of the Tribe <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> in whose <ns0:hi>Line</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Kingdom</ns0:hi> held unto the Captivity. (<ns0:hi>and his Brethren</ns0:hi>) the Brethren of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> are here mentioned, being the Heads of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Nation</ns0:hi>: Christ descended from <ns0:hi>Iudah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3. And Judas begat Phares and Sarah of Ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mar and Phares begat Esrom, and Esrom be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gat Aram.<ns0:note place="bottom">That <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Pharez</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zarah</ns0:hi> (they were Twins begot of <ns0:hi>Thamar</ns0:hi> his Daughter-in-Law, the relict of his Son <ns0:hi>Er</ns0:hi> whom God slew <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 38.7.) appeareth from <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 38.27, 28, 29, 30. That <ns0:hi>Pharez</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Ezrom,</ns0:hi> appeareth from <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> 4.18. and 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 2.5. and from the same Texts appears also that <ns0:hi>Ezrom</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Aram, Ruth</ns0:hi> 4.19. 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 2.9. where he is called <ns0:hi>Ram,</ns0:hi> some may possibly be offended that amongst all the Ancestors of Christ, there are but three <ns0:hi>Women</ns0:hi> na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med, and all of th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>m such as had a great <ns0:hi>stain</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>blot</ns0:hi> up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on their <ns0:hi>Reputation.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Thamar,</ns0:hi> the Mother of <ns0:hi>Pharez</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zara</ns0:hi> was blotted with <ns0:hi>Incest,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharez</ns0:hi> was one of the Children begot in that <ns0:hi>Incest. Rahab</ns0:hi> also is mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5. whom the Scripture calleth an <ns0:hi>Harlot, Iosh.</ns0:hi> 2.1. and <ns0:hi>Bathsheba</ns0:hi> was stained with <ns0:hi>Adultery.</ns0:hi> But we ought to consider, 1. That (abating Original Corruption which we indeed all derive from our Parents) no man deriveth any intrinsick badness from the Vice of his Parents, tho he may derive, a blot upon his <ns0:hi>Honour</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Reputation,</ns0:hi> from it. 2. That this was one degree of our Saviours <ns0:hi>Humiliation.</ns0:hi> 3. That it was no way incongruous, that he who came into the World to dye for great Sinners, should be born of some that were such.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4. And Aram begat Aminadab, and Aminadab begat Naasson, and Naasson begat Salmon.<ns0:note place="bottom">This exactly agreeth with the Old Testament, <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> 4.19.20. 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 2.10.11. only it is there said, that <ns0:hi>Naasson,</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>Prince of the Children of Iudah, Num.</ns0:hi> 1.7. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 2, 3. and <ns0:hi>Salmon</ns0:hi> is there called <ns0:hi>Salma.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5. And Salmon begat Boaz of Rachab, and Boaz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6. And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 12.</ns0:note> Jesse begat David the King—<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">This agreeth with <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> 4.22. and 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 16.2.2.15. Here now ariseth the first Difficulty we meet with in this <ns0:hi>Genealogy,</ns0:hi> and it is rather an appearance of a Difficulty than a real one. <ns0:hi>Salmon</ns0:hi> being the Son of <ns0:hi>Ami<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nadab,</ns0:hi> who was the Prince of the Children of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> time, <ns0:hi>Salmon</ns0:hi> cannot be imagined to have lived la<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter than in the times of <ns0:hi>Ioshua. Booz</ns0:hi> seemeth to have lived in <ns0:hi>Elies</ns0:hi> time, which (if <ns0:hi>Chronologers</ns0:hi> count right) was 300 years after, here are but four men named to take up these years. <ns0:hi>Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Iesse. Ans.</ns0:hi> The World accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to <ns0:hi>Chronologers</ns0:hi> wanted but five of 2500 years old, when the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> (under the Conduct of <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi>) entred into <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi>: We will suppose <ns0:hi>Salmon,</ns0:hi> to have then been a young man. <ns0:hi>Eli</ns0:hi> is by them said to have lived about the 2810th. So that the distance is 315 years. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> is said to have been born in the 2860th. So as from <ns0:hi>Salmon</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> are 365 years Admit <ns0:hi>Salmon, Boaz, Obed</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iesse</ns0:hi> to have each of them lived an <ns0:hi>hundred years,</ns0:hi> or upward and this is no Difficulty. Nor can be any absurdity in admitting this, if we consider the Age, and Vigor of Persons in that age of the World. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> (tho a man spent with <ns0:hi>Travels</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Battels</ns0:hi>) lived 120 years, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 34.7. <ns0:hi>Caleb</ns0:hi> at 85 years was strong, and as fit <ns0:hi>for War,</ns0:hi> as ever <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 14.11.12. If we allow these four men the Life of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> they might live 480 years, which might allow to each of them 15 or 16 years apiece for the Concurrency of their Lives with their Parents, yet 365 years might be well allowed for all their time: Nor is it unreasonable for us to suppose that God might allow those whom he intended thus to dignifie a something longer Life, then the ordinary sort of men lived in that age of the World. So as the thing be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing neither naturally impo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sible (for in our Age we see par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticular Persons live upward of an hundred years) nor <ns0:hi>morally improbable,</ns0:hi> and directly affirmed in three or four Texts, they must have a great mind to quarrel with a <ns0:hi>Divine Revelation</ns0:hi> who quarrel the Truth of it upon such a pretence: Especially considering that the Lives of men in our declining, and De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />baucht age of the World, are no measures by which we can guess at the Lives of extraordinary Persons who lived near three thousand years ago. [<ns0:hi>David the King</ns0:hi>] possibly that term is added to distinguish the <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> here intended, from others of the same name, or because he was the <ns0:hi>first King of the Tribe of Iudah</ns0:hi> to whom the Scepter of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> was promised, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 49 10. Or the <ns0:hi>first King not given to the Israelites in wrath,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> was upon their murmuring against <ns0:hi>Samuel,</ns0:hi> or to shew that <ns0:hi>Christ descended from that Family,</ns0:hi> to whom the Promise of the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> was made, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 23.5. and a <ns0:hi>Kingdom</ns0:hi> established for ever. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 89.36, 37. Thus our <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> hath given us the Names in his first <ns0:hi>Period,</ns0:hi> or fourteen Gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rations. <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac, Iacob, Iudas, Pharez, Ezrom, Aram, Aminadab, Naasson, Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Iesse, Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:217" />6 And David the King begat Solomon of her <ns0:hi>that had been the wife</ns0:hi> of Uriah.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi> was not the eldest Child of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Bathsheba,</ns0:hi> that dyed, 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 12.22, 23. He was born after <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> had taken <ns0:hi>Bathsheba</ns0:hi> (who had been the Wife of <ns0:hi>Vriah</ns0:hi>) for his Wife, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25. compared with 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 11.27.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Chro. 3.10.</ns0:note> Solomon begat Roboam, and Roboam begat Abia; and Abia begat Asa.<ns0:note place="bottom">This exactly agrees with the History of the <ns0:hi>Old Testament,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 11.43. (where he is called <ns0:hi>Rehoboam</ns0:hi>) he Reigned but seventeen years and dyed, 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 14.21. and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31. <ns0:hi>Abijam</ns0:hi> his Son Reigned in his stead, he is here called <ns0:hi>Abia.</ns0:hi> But we shall observe frequent alteration of Names, both as to the <ns0:hi>final Terminations,</ns0:hi> and where the quiescent Letters in <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> fall into the Name. <ns0:hi>Abia</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Abijam</ns0:hi> Reigned but <ns0:hi>three years,</ns0:hi> and was succeeded by <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi> his Son, 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 15.2.8. <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi> Reigned forty one years, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 16.13. So as these three Princes Reigned <ns0:hi>sixty years.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And Asa begat Josaphat, and Josaphat be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gate Joram, and Joram begat Ozias.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iehosaphat</ns0:hi> here called <ns0:hi>Iosaphat,</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> (they having no Letter to express the Hebrew <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> by) was the Son of <ns0:hi>Asa,</ns0:hi> a good Son of a good Father, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 17.1, 2. he Reign<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed twenty five years, 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 22.42. <ns0:hi>Iehoram</ns0:hi> (here called <ns0:hi>Ioram</ns0:hi>) succeeded him in his Kingdom, he slew <ns0:hi>his Brethren, he walked in the ways of Ahab,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 21.2.6. he Reign<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed but eight years, lived, and dyed wickedly, and was buried infamously, 2 <ns0:hi>Chr.</ns0:hi> 21.20. But here ariseth another Difficulty from what is said, <ns0:hi>Ioram begate Ozias.</ns0:hi> It is certain that he did not beget him <ns0:hi>immediately,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>Vzziah</ns0:hi> was the fourth from <ns0:hi>Ioram. Iehoram</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ioram</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Ahaziah,</ns0:hi> he was his youngest Son, he lived but one year as <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 21.1, 2. then <ns0:hi>Athaliah</ns0:hi> usurped the Kingdom for six years, not coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting her Usurpation. <ns0:hi>Ioash</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Ahaziah</ns0:hi> Reigned for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty years, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 24.1. He dies, 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 12.21. And <ns0:hi>Ama<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ziah</ns0:hi> his Son Reigned in his stead, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 26.1. He was the Father of <ns0:hi>Vzziah</ns0:hi> called <ns0:hi>Azariah,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 14.21. So that when it is said: That <ns0:hi>Ioram</ns0:hi> begate <ns0:hi>Oziah,</ns0:hi> we must only understand, that <ns0:hi>Vzziah</ns0:hi> lineally descended from <ns0:hi>Ioram,</ns0:hi> thus, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1. Christ is called the <ns0:hi>Son of David, The Son of Abraham.</ns0:hi> Thus the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> said, <ns0:hi>We have Abraham to our Father,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> is said to be <ns0:hi>of the Daughters</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Aaron, Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.5. But it is a greater Question, why the Evangelist leaves out <ns0:hi>Aha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ziah, Ioash</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Amaziah</ns0:hi> who were all three lawful Princes, and rightly descended from the <ns0:hi>Family of David.</ns0:hi> To pass by various Conjectures, the best account I find given of it is this. 1. It is manifest the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> had a design to divide all the Generations from <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> into three <ns0:hi>Periods.</ns0:hi> The first of which should contain the <ns0:hi>Growing State</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Common-Wealth,</ns0:hi> till it came at the heighth which was in <ns0:hi>Davids</ns0:hi> time. The second should contain its <ns0:hi>Flourishing State</ns0:hi>; which was from <ns0:hi>Davids</ns0:hi> time till the first carrying in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to Captivity. The third should contain <ns0:hi>its declining State,</ns0:hi> from the first carrying them into Captivity to the coming of Christ. 2. He designed to reduce all the Generations in each Period to fourteen, this appeareth from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17. Now altho the first <ns0:hi>Period</ns0:hi> contained exactly fourteen Descents or Gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rations, yet in the second there was manifestly seventeen, so as the Evangelist was obliged to leave out three to bring them to the number of fourteen; now tho it be a little too Curious to inquire why the Evangelist chose to leave out these three: <ns0:hi>Ahaziah, Ioash,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Amaziah,</ns0:hi> rather then any other three, yet there is the probable good Account of it given by lear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned Men, who have waded into these Speculations. <ns0:hi>Ahaziah</ns0:hi> was the Son of <ns0:hi>Iehoram</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Athaliah</ns0:hi> the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Ahab,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 21.6. <ns0:hi>Ioash</ns0:hi> her <ns0:hi>Grand-child, Amaziah</ns0:hi> her <ns0:hi>Great Grand-child.</ns0:hi> Now God had cursed the house of <ns0:hi>Ahab,</ns0:hi> and threatned to root out all his House, 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 21.21. This (as is supposed) made the <ns0:hi>Evangelist,</ns0:hi> who was necessitated to leave out three to bring the <ns0:hi>Generations</ns0:hi> to fourteen, rather to chuse to leave out these <ns0:hi>Princes,</ns0:hi> who were of <ns0:hi>Ahabs</ns0:hi> half Blood, then any others. If any say why then did he not leave out more? Besides that he was not obliged any other way (then as he would keep to his <ns0:hi>number</ns0:hi> to leave out these) he knew Gods <ns0:hi>Threatnings</ns0:hi> of Children, for the sins of Parents, usually terminate in the third, and fourth Generation.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And Ozias begat of Joatham, and Joatham begate Achaz, and Achaz begat Ezekias.<ns0:note place="bottom">That <ns0:hi>Iotham</ns0:hi> succeeded his Father <ns0:hi>Ozias</ns0:hi> and Reigned six<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teen years, agreeth with 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 26.23. and that <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> his Son succeeded him, agreeth with 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 28.1. he also Reigned sixteen years, <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> his Son Reigned in his stead, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 28.27. Some here have cavilled at the Truth of the History of <ns0:hi>Holy-writ,</ns0:hi> because it appeareth from 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 16.2. that <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> dyed at thirty six years of Age, and that <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> began to Reign at twenty five years of Age, doth also appear from 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 29.1. whence it appeareth that <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> must be <ns0:hi>born</ns0:hi> when his Father was but <ns0:hi>eleven years of Age,</ns0:hi> which they think improbable: But those who will question the Truth of what we have so good a Proof of, as the Revelation of <ns0:hi>Holy-writ</ns0:hi> is, are obliged not only to tell us of things in it that are improbable to their apprehensions, but ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther in Nature impossible, or at least in consistent with some other piece of <ns0:hi>Divine Revelation.</ns0:hi> Of the latter sort, we hear of nothing objected in this Case. Now tho with us it be not or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dinary for Persons at that Age to beget Children, yet that it is not impossible in Nature, nor more then hath happened in the World sometimes, <ns0:hi>Spanhemius</ns0:hi> hath largely proved in his <ns0:hi>Dubia Evangelica, Dub.</ns0:hi> 5. and that by no less Authorities then those of <ns0:hi>Hierome</ns0:hi> amongst the Ancients, and the learned <ns0:hi>Scaliger</ns0:hi> amongst the more Modern Writers, it is what may be. The Scripture telleth us it was so, that is enough for us, tho it be not a thing very ordinary.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 20.21. 1 Chron. 3.13.</ns0:note> Ezekias begat Manasses, and Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nasses begat Amon, and Amon begat Josiah.<ns0:note place="bottom">All this exactly agreeth with the Scriptures of the Old Testament, these three Princes in a lineal Descent immedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ately succeeded each other, <ns0:hi>Manasseth,</ns0:hi> Reigning 55. <ns0:hi>Amon,</ns0:hi> 2. and <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> thirty one years, all together eighty eight years.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 23.34. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 24.1. 2 Chron. 36.4.</ns0:note> Josias <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Some <ns0:hi>read begate</ns0:hi> Jakim, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> Jakim <ns0:hi>be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gate</ns0:hi> Jeconiah.</ns0:note> begat Jeconias and his Brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon.<ns0:note place="bottom">In this <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> (who ever he was) determined the <ns0:hi>Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelists</ns0:hi> second <ns0:hi>Period</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>fourteen Generations.</ns0:hi> But there is much Dispute, both about the <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> who is here menti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />oned, and the Sons of <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> as they are reckoned up, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.15. where it is said. <ns0:hi>The Sons of Iosiah were the first born Iehanan, The second Iehojakim, The third Zedekiah.</ns0:hi> The fourth <ns0:hi>Shallum,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 23.31. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.1. It is plain that <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz</ns0:hi> succeeded <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> his Father: It is certain that amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> it was very ordinary for Persons to have two Names; thus King <ns0:hi>Vzziah</ns0:hi> in the Book of <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> called <ns0:hi>Azariah,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 14.21. Most if not all of <ns0:hi>Iosiahs</ns0:hi> Sons had two Names, it is plain that <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz</ns0:hi> his eldest Son is the same who in 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.15. is called <ns0:hi>Iohanan,</ns0:hi> but he Reign<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed but three Months, probably set up by the People, and put down by <ns0:hi>Pharaoh Necho,</ns0:hi> in a Battle against whom <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> was slain, he pursuing his Victory put him down and set up <ns0:hi>Eliakim</ns0:hi> his next Brother, calling him <ns0:hi>Iehoiachim,</ns0:hi> as he is call<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.15. he Reigned <ns0:hi>eleven</ns0:hi> years, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.5. The <ns0:hi>King of Babylon</ns0:hi> puts him down, and setteth up <ns0:hi>Iehojachin</ns0:hi> his Son, who is also called <ns0:hi>Ieconiah,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />niah,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.9. he Reigned but three Months, and ten days, and the <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> fetcheth him away, and sets up his Uncle <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> (called also <ns0:hi>Mattaniah</ns0:hi>) he Reigned <ns0:hi>eleven years,</ns0:hi> as appeareth by 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. then the whole Body of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were carried away Captive into <ns0:hi>Ba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bylon.</ns0:hi> We do not read either in the Book of <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Chro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nicles,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>Shallum (Iosiahs</ns0:hi> fourth Son) ever Reigned, yet it should seem that he did, by <ns0:hi>Ieremiah,</ns0:hi> 22. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. Some think that he was set up in stead of <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz,</ns0:hi> when he was carried away. But the Scripture saith nothing of it, nor is it very probable that the Conqueror should skip over the <ns0:hi>Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cond</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Third</ns0:hi> Son, and set up the <ns0:hi>Fourth.</ns0:hi> But it is not my present Concern, to inquire after <ns0:hi>Shallum,</ns0:hi> but only after <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> mentioned in this Verse, and the other <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> mentioned in the 12 Verse, as the Head of those Generations which make up the last <ns0:hi>Period.</ns0:hi> As to this <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> the most probable Opinion is, that it was <ns0:hi>Iehojakim,</ns0:hi> who was also called <ns0:hi>Ieconiah,</ns0:hi> and that the <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. was <ns0:hi>Iehojakin,</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Iehojakim.</ns0:hi> In this I find some of the best Interpreters acquiescing, nor indeed is there any great Difficulty, in allowing <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> the Father, as well as <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hojachin</ns0:hi> the Son to be called <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> (so near are the Names akin, and the <ns0:hi>signification</ns0:hi> of both the same) but then the Que<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stion is, how <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> could be said to beget <ns0:hi>Iehojachim, About</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>time</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>the carrying into the Captivity of Babylon</ns0:hi>; for it appeareth by 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.5. That <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> was twenty five years <ns0:hi>Old when he began to Reign, and he Reigned eleven years</ns0:hi>; and in his time was the first carrying into <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> so that there must be thirty seven years betwixt the begetting of <ns0:hi>Ieho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jakim</ns0:hi> and the first <ns0:hi>Transportation into Babylon.</ns0:hi> The Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gent of our Bibles tell us of another Reading, <ns0:hi>Iosias</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Ia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />kim (Iakim</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iehojakim</ns0:hi> are the same) and <ns0:hi>Iakim</ns0:hi> begate <ns0:hi>Iechoniah</ns0:hi> (that is <ns0:hi>Iehojakim.</ns0:hi>) <ns0:hi>Beza</ns0:hi> thinks this the truest reading taken out of an old Copy of <ns0:hi>R. Stephens,</ns0:hi> magnified by <ns0:hi>Stapulensis</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Bucor.</ns0:hi> But he thinks it should be thus, <ns0:hi>Iosias begate Iakim, and his Brethren</ns0:hi> (for we know that <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> had four Sons) and <ns0:hi>Iakim</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> (that is, <ns0:hi>Iehojakin) about the time of the carrying into the Cap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tivity of Babylon.</ns0:hi> For <ns0:hi>Iehojakin</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> was not nine years old when himself was carried away, and his Father was carried away before [<ns0:hi>about the carrying away into Babylon</ns0:hi>] The <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> Preposition <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> doth not signifie any determinate certain time, but doth include sometimes many, and distinct ti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>es as it must do here, for <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> began to Reign at eight years old, and Reigned thirty one years, so that he dyed at thirty nine years of Age, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 34. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz</ns0:hi> (or <ns0:hi>Iohanan</ns0:hi>) his eldest Son succeeded him at twenty three years old, so he must be born when <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> was sixteen years of Age. <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> began to Reign at twenty five years of Age. <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> at one and twenty, as appeareth from 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.1, 5, 11. so that <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> must be but about nine years old when his Father dyed, which was not twelve years before <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> was carried into <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> as appeareth by the History, 2 <ns0:hi>Chr.</ns0:hi> 36. Thus, the Persons in this <ns0:hi>Period,</ns0:hi> which) was the flourishing time of the Kingdom of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi>) are fourteen: <ns0:hi>Solomon, Rehoboam, Abia, Asa, Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hosaphat, Ioram, Vzziah, Iotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nasses, Amon, Iosiah, Iehojachim,</ns0:hi> only here is no mention made of <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz</ns0:hi> his Reign, who was <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>eldest Son,</ns0:hi> who it may be is not mentioned by the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi>: Either, because <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> (here called <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi>) was a <ns0:hi>second Son</ns0:hi> of the same Father, or in regard of his short Reign (for it was but three <ns0:hi>Months and odd days</ns0:hi>) or it may be, because in all Probability he was Tumultuously set up by the Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, and not fixed in his Throne, before he was turned out by the Conqueror <ns0:hi>Pharaoh Necho,</ns0:hi> nor do we read of any Sons he left, to be sure he left none who could succeed him in the Throne, for <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> was set up, and his Son <ns0:hi>Iehojachin</ns0:hi> succeeded him, as the History telleth us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:218" />12 And after they were brought to Babylon, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 24.6.</ns0:note> Jeconia begat Salathiel, and Salathiel begat <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezra 3.2.</ns0:note> Zorobabel.<ns0:note place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> is generally thought to be <ns0:hi>Iehojakin</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Iehojakim,</ns0:hi> he is called <ns0:hi>Ieconiah,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.16. as well as <ns0:hi>Iehojakin,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.8. so also <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 24.1. he is called <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Iehojakim,</ns0:hi> that this <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lathiel,</ns0:hi> appeareth from 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.17. It is here objected that God said concerning this <ns0:hi>Ieconiah,</ns0:hi> called also <ns0:hi>Coniah, Ier.</ns0:hi> 22.30. <ns0:hi>write you this man Childless,</ns0:hi> how then did he beget <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi>; but it is easily answered, for that Verse, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 22.30. will expound it self. <ns0:hi>Write you this man Childless, a man that shall not prosper in his days, for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the Throne of David, and ruling any more in Iudah:</ns0:hi> So as that Text is plainly to be understood <ns0:hi>without a Child that shall actually succeed</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Crown,</ns0:hi> for the Text it self supposeth that he should have <ns0:hi>seed</ns0:hi> but none that should <ns0:hi>prosper, sitting upon the Throne of David,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>ruling in Iudah,</ns0:hi> which the Scripture, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36. justifieth, for the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> set up <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> his Uncle in his stead, who was the last <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> in the eleventh year of whose Reign the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were all carried Captive. This <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi> had eight Sons as we read, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.17.18. <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> is there reckoned as his <ns0:hi>second Son</ns0:hi> (possibly <ns0:hi>Assir</ns0:hi> dyed young, or at least Childless) so as the right of the Crown was in <ns0:hi>Salathiel,</ns0:hi> who is the Person alone here named. But how <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> is here said, to have <ns0:hi>begot Zorobabel</ns0:hi> is yet a greater Difficulty; for, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.19. it is said: The Sons of <ns0:hi>Pedajah</ns0:hi> (not of <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lathiel</ns0:hi>) were <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Shimei,</ns0:hi> if <ns0:hi>Zorobabel</ns0:hi> were the Son of <ns0:hi>Pedajah,</ns0:hi> how could he be the Son of <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi>? Seve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Answers are given to this. Some think that <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause he descended lineally from <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> is called his <ns0:hi>Son,</ns0:hi> which were a sufficient Answer if the Supposition were true, that <ns0:hi>Zorobabel</ns0:hi> were lineally descended from <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi>: But that it is not, for according to 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.18. <ns0:hi>Pedajah</ns0:hi> was not the <ns0:hi>Son,</ns0:hi> but the Brother of <ns0:hi>Salathiel.</ns0:hi> Others think that <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lathiel</ns0:hi> is here said to have begot <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> because <ns0:hi>Zorobabel succeeded him in the Kingdom,</ns0:hi> but as that is a strange <ns0:hi>Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pretation</ns0:hi> of the word <ns0:hi>begat,</ns0:hi> So neither was <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> tho possibly the Title of the Crown was in him, as the Great Grand-child of <ns0:hi>Iosiah,</ns0:hi> nor did ever <ns0:hi>Zorobabel</ns0:hi> as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sume the Crown that we read of. Whereas others say, that there were two <ns0:hi>Zorobabels</ns0:hi>; and that this Son was the adopted Son of <ns0:hi>Salathiel,</ns0:hi> both these things are suggested without Proof. The most probable Opinion which I perceive the best <ns0:hi>Interpreters</ns0:hi> acquie<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ce in, is, That <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> dying without issue <ns0:hi>Pedajah</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Brother</ns0:hi> married his Wife according to the Law of God, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 25.5. and begat <ns0:hi>Zorobabel</ns0:hi> of her that had been the Wife of <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi>; and thence it is said <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lathiel</ns0:hi> begat him. <ns0:hi>Pedajah</ns0:hi> so raising up seed to his <ns0:hi>Bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther</ns0:hi> according to the Law aforesaid. To this it is objected by some, That the Law was, <ns0:hi>That the Child should succeed in the name of the Brother that was dead:</ns0:hi> So that if this were the Sense it should not have been, <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Salathiel.</ns0:hi> The Answer to this, is not Difficult: For <ns0:hi>to succeed in the name of the Brother that is dead,</ns0:hi> doth not signifie to be called by the very name with which he was called, but to be denominated his Son, as if be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gotten by him. And this is Evident from <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> 4 10. where <ns0:hi>Boaz</ns0:hi> hath these words, <ns0:hi>Ruth the Moabitess, the Wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my Wife, to raise up the Name of the dead upon his Inheritance, that the Name of the dead, be not cut off from among his Brethren.</ns0:hi> Yet <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. <ns0:hi>Boaz</ns0:hi> having a Son by <ns0:hi>Ruth,</ns0:hi> did not call his name <ns0:hi>Mahlon,</ns0:hi> by the name of his Father, but <ns0:hi>Obed.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And Zorobabel begat Abiud, and Abiud be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gat Eliakim, and Eliakim begat Azor.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And Azor begat Sadoc, and Sadoc begat Achim, and Achim begat Eliud.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And Eliud begate Eleazar, and Eleazar be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gate Matthan, and Matthan begate Jacob.<ns0:note place="bottom">Here are divers Objections made to this last part of the <ns0:hi>Ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nealogy,</ns0:hi> and in a great measure caused from the difference be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tween <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi>; but I shall not attempt any Recon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciliation of those Differences, till I come to <ns0:hi>Luke, ch.</ns0:hi> 3. There is no <ns0:hi>Abiud</ns0:hi> reckoned amongst the Sons of <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.19.20. and for the others named, we have no certain Ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />count of them, in any part of the Holy-writ. From the time of <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> were above five hundred years to the <ns0:hi>Birth</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>: Of which seventy were spent in the <ns0:hi>Captivity of Ba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bylon, Zorobabel</ns0:hi> was alive at the end of the <ns0:hi>Captivity, Ezra</ns0:hi> 5.2. and, as it appears, the <ns0:hi>Ruler</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>the Iews</ns0:hi> tho not under the <ns0:hi>Title,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>stile</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> For <ns0:hi>Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Mathan,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob.</ns0:hi> Tho we have no men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of them, in any <ns0:hi>Canonical Books</ns0:hi> of Holy-writ, but only this, yet <ns0:hi>Mathew's</ns0:hi> Credit in the Church of God, ought to out-weigh any other Writings, pretending any thing contrary to what he saith; we are therefore obliged to believe they all lineally descended from <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> but living in a private State, and Condition, and Holy-writ not extending its History be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yond <ns0:hi>Zorobabels</ns0:hi> time (the time when the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> came out of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi>) it is no wonder that we have no better means then we have, from Holy-writ to know their lineal Descent from the <ns0:hi>Royal Family.</ns0:hi> That <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> in what he wrote was guided by the unerring Spirit, and that he had Rolls of <ns0:hi>Pedegrees</ns0:hi> which we want, we have reason to believe. This is enough for us Christians, who own the Books of the <ns0:hi>New</ns0:hi> as well as the <ns0:hi>Old Testament,</ns0:hi> to be wrote by Persons divinely inspired, so as to them we have nothing to do, but to reconcile <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> both, whom we own to have had the same in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fallible Inspiration and Direction. If <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Pagans</ns0:hi> argue from any other <ns0:hi>Topick</ns0:hi> then this, it is enough to tell them, That the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> kept exact Genealogies, and more especially as to the Descents in the Tribes of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> that they might never be at loss as to the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> whom they expected, as the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> nor yet as to the true <ns0:hi>High-Priest.</ns0:hi> Tho these <ns0:hi>Records,</ns0:hi> and Rolls of <ns0:hi>Genealogy</ns0:hi> be now lost, yet we have no reason to believe they were so in <ns0:hi>Mathews</ns0:hi> time, of which Genealogies (as to this part) doubtless what <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew</ns0:hi> saith was but a Copy, directed by that Holy Spirit, by which he was inspired.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And Jacob begat Joseph the Husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus who is called Christ.<ns0:note place="bottom">How <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> cometh to make <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Heli,</ns0:hi> we shall inquire (if God please) when we come to his third Chapter: But from this Verse ariseth a very <ns0:hi>Grave</ns0:hi> Question, <ns0:hi>viz. How, or wherefore, the Evangelist in deriving the Pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />degree of Christ, bringeth the line down to</ns0:hi> Joseph, <ns0:hi>from whom our Saviour did not descend,</ns0:hi> being no <ns0:hi>flesh of his Flesh.</ns0:hi> Christ being the promised <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Propechy, Isa.</ns0:hi> 7.14. must be, and was fulfilled in him. <ns0:hi>A Virgin shall con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive and bear a Son, and thou shalt call his name</ns0:hi> Emanuel. Now if <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> were not the true, but only the <ns0:hi>Legal</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed</ns0:hi> Father of Christ: What had the Evangelist to do with his <ns0:hi>Genealogy</ns0:hi>? Many Answers are given to this, some think that the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> accommodateth himself to the <ns0:hi>Vulgar Opi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nion,</ns0:hi> they took him generally for the true and natural Son of <ns0:hi>Ioseph.</ns0:hi> They said, <ns0:hi>Is not this the Carpenters Son?</ns0:hi> But then the Holy Spirit, must have attempted to have proved a Conclusion true, from a <ns0:hi>Medium</ns0:hi> that was false, which must by no means be allowed: Besides, neither could this be <ns0:hi>Mathews</ns0:hi> design, who afterwards relateth the <ns0:hi>Mystery</ns0:hi> of our Saviours <ns0:hi>Incarnation</ns0:hi> plain enough; and tells us <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18. That <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>found with Child before Ioseph, and she came together,</ns0:hi> o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers therefore say that amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Genealogies</ns0:hi> of Women use not to be reckoned. How universally true that is, I cannot tell, generally it is (very probable) as being usual almost with all Nations to reckon Descents from the <ns0:hi>Males.</ns0:hi> In the present Case it is granted by most that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> deriveth the Descent of <ns0:hi>Mary.</ns0:hi> In the present Case, it seemeth of high Concern that the <ns0:hi>Genealogy</ns0:hi> both of <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> should be counted: Tho our Saviours being the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> could not have been proved from his being the <ns0:hi>Son of Ioseph,</ns0:hi> for then he could not have been the <ns0:hi>Son of a Virgin</ns0:hi> (yet admitting the Jewish error in that Case, not knowing the Mystery of Christs Incarnation) <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> by their own Confession was confirmed to be the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> because <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> was so: On the other side, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> deriving <ns0:hi>Maries Genealogy</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and affirming Christ to be born of a <ns0:hi>Virgin espoused,</ns0:hi> confirmed him to all the World to be both the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> descending from <ns0:hi>Mary a Virgin,</ns0:hi> that was a Daughter to one who was the Son of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and also the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> in whom the Propechy was fulfilled, of a <ns0:hi>Virgins conceiving and bearing a Son</ns0:hi>; so that by the reckoning of the Generation of two Persons, both of which were lineally descended from <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> he was proved to be the <ns0:hi>Son of David</ns0:hi> both to the generality of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who could not deny but <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> was so, and to all believers both <ns0:hi>Iews and Gentiles,</ns0:hi> to whom God should give to believe the My<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stery of the <ns0:hi>Incarnation</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Conception of the Holy Ghost.</ns0:hi> This to me seems a sufficient reason for the reckoning up our Saviours descent from <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> both by <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> and Mother. Which is advantaged by considering that <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> was not only the <ns0:hi>reputed Father,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>legal Father</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> and altho his being not the <ns0:hi>Natural,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>legal Father</ns0:hi> of Christ, will not prove him the <ns0:hi>Son of David, further</ns0:hi> then to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> who would have him to be the <ns0:hi>Natural Son of Ioseph,</ns0:hi> yet the <ns0:hi>Genealogy</ns0:hi> reckoned from <ns0:hi>Abraham to Ioseph</ns0:hi> will prove <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> (whom they judged Christs natural Father) so as they had nothing to say against that, and the other parts of this Gospel, and this Chapter indeed with the Genealogy of <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> will prove that he was both the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> and the true <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> as a Son <ns0:hi>born of a Virgin.</ns0:hi> Whereas some say that <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> was of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> and think to prove it by her being Cousen to <ns0:hi>Elizabeth,</ns0:hi> who is expressly called a <ns0:hi>Daughter of Aaron, Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.1. Besides that <ns0:hi>Luke ch.</ns0:hi> 3. plainly proveth her of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and of the Family of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> the Proof is by no means sufficient, for altho the Law, <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 36.8.9. for the avoiding of a Confu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion of Inheritances, commanded them to <ns0:hi>Marry within their Tribes,</ns0:hi> yet this Law concerned not the Daughters of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> for that <ns0:hi>Tribe</ns0:hi> had no Inheritance as the rest. So as that kindred might easily be, tho <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> was not of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> but of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> as indeed she was. But leaving this Question, let us come to the words of the Verse. And <ns0:hi>Ia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cob begat Ioseph, the Husband of Mary,</ns0:hi> that is, the <ns0:hi>espoused Husband of Mary.</ns0:hi> Espousals make a Marriage before God: The Angel afterward saith to <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> (but yet espoused) <ns0:hi>Fear not to take unto thee Mary thy Wife.</ns0:hi> And he was soon after the <ns0:hi>Legal, Actual</ns0:hi> Husband of <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi>: Of <ns0:hi>whom was born Iesus, who was called Christ,</ns0:hi> that Person who was <ns0:hi>called Iesus</ns0:hi> by the Direction of the <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> as we shall by and by see who was also called <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> which as we said signifieth <ns0:hi>Anointed,</ns0:hi> and the same with <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi> It is observed by some that the Name <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> was given to <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> (because of their anointing) before the Captivity, but to none after, till he came who was <ns0:hi>the Christ,</ns0:hi> God by that Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidence (if the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> would have understood it) pointing out to them, that the Person was now come who was promised them under the Notion of the <ns0:hi>Messiah, Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.25 26. and whom they expected, as appeareth from <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.41. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 4.25. and no longer to be expected.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:218" />17 So all the Generations from Abraham to David <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> fourteen Generations; And from Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid to the carrying away into Babylon, <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> four<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teen Generations, and from the carrying away into Babylon, unto Christ <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> fourteen Gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rations.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Evangelist for reasons which we cannot fathom, re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duceth our <ns0:hi>Saviour's</ns0:hi> Progenitors to <ns0:hi>fourteen</ns0:hi> in each <ns0:hi>Period</ns0:hi> of the Jewish State, and in the first <ns0:hi>Period</ns0:hi> determining with <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> there were no more. In the second, he leaveth out three Kings descended from the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Ahab.</ns0:hi> In the third which was <ns0:hi>from the Captivity to Christ,</ns0:hi> there were doubtless more, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> reckoneth up twenty four (taking in <ns0:hi>Christ for one</ns0:hi>) and agreeth in very few with <ns0:hi>Mathew,</ns0:hi> who was forced to leave out some to keep to his number of fourteen. Nor doth <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> speak any thing false, or contradictious to <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> in saying there were fourteen tho there were more. Besides, there might be many more Progenitors of <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> then <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> whose Pedegree <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> deriveth.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Now the Birth of Jesus Christ was <ns0:note place="margin">Luk. 1.27.</ns0:note> on this wise, when as his mother Mary was espou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed, to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the holy Ghost.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Evangelist prefaceth this extraordinary Birth of our Saviour in this manner.
