Now, <ns0:hi>the Birth of Iesus Christ was on this wise,</ns0:hi> not in the ordinary Course and manner in which Children are conceived and brought forth into the World, but in this wonderful manner <ns0:hi>[when his mother Mary was espoused to Ioseph.] Betrothing,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Espousing,</ns0:hi> was nothing else but a Solemn promise of Marriage made by two Persons each to o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, at such distance of time, as they agreed upon. It was a Decent usage approved of (if not ordained) by God, as appears by <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 20.7. That we are obliged still to use it, I dare not say, it might be a prudential Order and Constitution of that State. There was nothing in it <ns0:hi>Typical,</ns0:hi> nothing to bring it under the Notion of a <ns0:hi>Carnal Ordinance,</ns0:hi> (as the Apostle calls some of their <ns0:hi>Ordinances</ns0:hi> relating to the Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship of God) It seemeth <ns0:hi>Equitable,</ns0:hi> that the Parties to be Married might have some Convenient time to think seriously of the great Change they are soon to make in their Lives, and more solemnly seek unto God for his Blessing upon them, as also that they might more freely Discourse together about their Houshold Affairs, and the Settlement of their Families, then the modesty of the Virgins of that age would otherwise have allowed them. It made them Man and Wife be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore God, tho they came not together for some time after: The distance of time, seemeth to have been left to the Agree<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of Parties, and Parents. In this Case we cannot cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainly assert the distance, but it appeareth to have been such, as that she was <ns0:hi>found with Child,</ns0:hi> before they came together. <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> knew what the Evangelist here asserteth, that it was <ns0:hi>by the Holy Ghost</ns0:hi>: For as she must know, that <ns0:hi>she had not known Man,</ns0:hi> as she told the <ns0:hi>Angel, Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.34. So the Angel had satisfied her, saying, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 35. <ns0:hi>The Holy Ghost shall come up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on thee, and the Power of the most high shall overshadow thee. Therefore also that Holy thing which shall be born of thee, shall be called the Son of God.</ns0:hi> It cannot be doubted but that she revealed this to some of her Friends, but how it came to be found, or who found it we are not told. <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> as yet had no such <ns0:hi>Revelation.</ns0:hi> God would have his Son to be born of a Virgin. 1. For the fulfilling of the Promise, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 7.14.2. Of <ns0:hi>the Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> that the Womb of the Virgin being sanctified by the Spirit of Holiness, there might be no Traduction of <ns0:hi>O<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riginal sin. Of a betrothed Virgin.</ns0:hi> 1. That he might not be under the Reproach of Illegitimacy. 2. Nor his Mother sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jected to the Punishment of the Judaical Law. 3. That <ns0:hi>Maries</ns0:hi> stock might be by her betrothed Husband. 4. That Christ might have a Guard in his Infancy.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Then Joseph her Husband being a just man, and not willing <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 24.1.</ns0:note> to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.<ns0:note place="bottom">It was found she was with Child (possibly her self, or some of her Friends told it to <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi>) her espoused Husband, it is plain from this Text, he came to the knowledge of it, for up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on it, the Evangelist saith, <ns0:hi>he was minded to put her away privily</ns0:hi>; had <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> at this time <ns0:hi>heard</ns0:hi> and believed, that the <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost had come upon her,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>the Power of the most High overshadowed her,</ns0:hi> being a good Man, he would not have entertained Thoughts of putting her away: But tho she had before received this <ns0:hi>Revelation,</ns0:hi> and might possibly have Communicated it to some of her Friends, yet it is manifest that her Husband <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> had not heard it, or at least was not easie to believe a thing of so unusal and extraordinary a Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture. That she was with Child, was Evident, how she came to be so, was as yet hidden from him, in Nature, and so incredi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble a thing, as it had argued too much of easiness of belief for him to have believed, had not <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> had (as afterward he had) a divine <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> for it, he therefore receiving such a Report, and finding it to be true, resolves to put her away in the privatest manner he could, rather then to expose her to a publick Shame, or to be made a publick Example. Their being betrothed was a thing publickly taken notice of, and he could not put her away so privately, but there must be Wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses of it, the meaning therefore must be as privately as the Nature of the thing would bear. <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> in this Case had the choice of three things. 1. <ns0:hi>He might</ns0:hi> notwithstanding this, <ns0:hi>have taken her to his House, as his Wife,</ns0:hi> for the Law of <ns0:hi>Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vorce</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>putting away,</ns0:hi> was but a Law giving a Liberty in Case of a discerned uncleanness to put away the Wife, it did not lay any under an Obligation so to do. 2. <ns0:hi>He might give her a Bill of Divorce, and</ns0:hi> leave her with her Friends. Now those skilled in the <ns0:hi>Iewsh Writings</ns0:hi> tell us this might be done; either, <ns0:hi>more privately</ns0:hi> before two or three Witnesses putting a Writing of that import into her Bosom, or more openly, and publickly before the Magistrate. 3. <ns0:hi>He might according to the Law, Deut.</ns0:hi> 22.23.24. <ns0:hi>&c. have brought her forth to be examined, whether she had only suffered a Rape, or had her self Consented.</ns0:hi> If it was done with her Consent she was by the Law to be stoned. Of these <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> in his first Thoughts upon the Matter, and before he rightly did understand the thing, chuseth the <ns0:hi>Second,</ns0:hi> and the milder part, and resolves to <ns0:hi>put her away,</ns0:hi> but in the most private manner the Law would in that Case allow him: He did this (saith the <ns0:hi>Vangelist</ns0:hi>) because he was <ns0:hi>a just Man,</ns0:hi> where the term <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifieth <ns0:hi>Equitable,</ns0:hi> in opposition to <ns0:hi>Severity</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rigour</ns0:hi>; nor ought any to say <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> in this shewed himself an unjust Man, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause by the Law, she ought to have been <ns0:hi>Stoned</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Death,</ns0:hi> for that is a mistake, supposing she had been with Child by man, yet if she had been forced, the man only wa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> to dye, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 22.28, 29, or she might have been with Child before her betrothing, in which Case she was only obliged to <ns0:hi>marry him</ns0:hi> that had so abased her: A kind, and Equitable man always presumeth the be<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, especially in a Case where Life is concerned, besides that no doubt <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> had by this time told <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> the Truth, and what the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> had said to her, to which (it being so incredible a thing as not to be believed, but upon a divine <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi>) tho <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> was not obliged having as yet no such <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> to give a present easie Faith, yet he might reasonably give so much Credit as to resolve upon the mildest Course he could take, tho he was willing also to avoid the blot upon himself by taking her to him for his Wife according to his Contract. God will not leave so good a man long unresolved what to do.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:219" />20 But while he thought on these things, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold, the Angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.<ns0:note place="bottom">What we have in this Verse assureth us, That <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> was not only inclined, by the Kindness and Benignity of his own natural Temper, and by his <ns0:hi>Charity</ns0:hi> to that moderate resolu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion he had taken up, but also more immediately influenced by God, who was now sending a Messenger to him to tell him, what he would have him to do in this Case. Whether this <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> was the Angel <ns0:hi>Gabriel,</ns0:hi> who <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> tells us <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.26. was sent to <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> to tell her <ns0:hi>that the Power of the most high should over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shadow her,</ns0:hi> or some other Angel, none can assert, an <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> it was. He appeareth to <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> while he was <ns0:hi>asleep,</ns0:hi> and in and by a <ns0:hi>Dream. By Dreams</ns0:hi> was one way by which God revealed his mind to People formerly, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 1.1. one of those ways by which God made himself known to Prophets, <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 12.6. and not to <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> only but to <ns0:hi>Pagan Princes</ns0:hi> sometimes, as appeareth by the instances we have in Scripture of the Dreams which <ns0:hi>Pharaoh</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezar</ns0:hi> both had Dreams, are either <ns0:hi>Natural,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Supernatural,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Preternatural.</ns0:hi> How to distinguish the former from the two latter, is not my work in this place, and possibly a difficult Task, especially in our times, when God having spoken to us by his Son, and given us his word as a per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect Rule, hath left off ordinary speaking to his <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Dreams</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Visions,</ns0:hi> tho not limited himself, but that he may sometimes so speak; we are assured of the Truth of a <ns0:hi>Divine Revelation</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> by this way of <ns0:hi>Dreams,</ns0:hi> while his Head was full of Thoughts what he was to do in this Case. God thinks of us, when we sleep, and one way or other will not be wanting to our Inquisition in sincerity to know his Will, in the difficult Cases of our Lives. The <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> saith unto <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seph, Ioseph, thou son of David</ns0:hi>; By which Compellation he lets him know, he was to be the <ns0:hi>Supposed</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Legal,</ns0:hi> tho not the <ns0:hi>Natural Father</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> who was by the Confes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion of all men, to be the Son of <ns0:hi>David. Fear not to take to thee Mary thy Wife.</ns0:hi> She that is thy betrothed Wife, and so thy Wife in my sight, thou hast espoused her, and called me to Witness, that thou wilt Consummate this Marriage with her in a due time<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and take her to thine House. I see what hath happened, which troubleth thy Thoughts, possibly thou art afraid lest thou should'st <ns0:hi>offend me,</ns0:hi> marrying one who appeareth unto thee, to be defiled, or thou art afraid of bringing a blot upon thy self if thou should'st Consummate this Marriage, but do not <ns0:hi>Fear</ns0:hi> any of these things, but go on, and <ns0:hi>Consummate</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> thy Marriage, she is not as thou supposest, or may'st Fear, defiled by Man, <ns0:hi>for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.</ns0:hi> That Holy thing, (as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> speaks) that humane Body which is in her Womb, is created in her, and is, <ns0:hi>of the Holy Ghost.</ns0:hi> The Holy Ghost by his Almighty creating Power, hath supplyed what is wanting from the help of the Creature<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> as to ordinary Productions of this Nature.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 1.31.</ns0:note> And she shall bring forth a Son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus: for he shall save his Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple from their sins.<ns0:note place="bottom">When the usual time of <ns0:hi>Women</ns0:hi> is accomplished, she shall <ns0:hi>bring forth a Son,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>thou shalt call his name Iesus.</ns0:hi> He shall not be thy <ns0:hi>Natural Son,</ns0:hi> but he shall be <ns0:hi>her Son,</ns0:hi> not begot by thee, but brought forth by her, so, <ns0:hi>Flesh</ns0:hi> of her <ns0:hi>Flesh, His namë shall be called Iesus</ns0:hi> by thee, or by his Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther. It is the Will of God thou should'st give him that Name. <ns0:hi>For he shall save his People from their Sins.</ns0:hi> It was the Custom of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> (Gods Ancient People) to give Names to their Children, either expressive of the <ns0:hi>Mercy</ns0:hi> which God had shewed them in giving them their <ns0:hi>Children,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>of the Duty</ns0:hi> which their Children did owe unto God. This name was given by God, expressing the <ns0:hi>Mercy of God</ns0:hi> to his People, in giving them this Child. For, <ns0:hi>he shall save his People from their Sins</ns0:hi> (saith the <ns0:hi>Angel) Iesus</ns0:hi> comes from an <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> word, which signifies <ns0:hi>Salvation. Ioshua</ns0:hi> had his Name from the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> word, because he was to be a Temporal Saviour to save the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> the whole Body of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> from the <ns0:hi>Canaanites</ns0:hi> their Enemies. This <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> was to save <ns0:hi>his People,</ns0:hi> all that should <ns0:hi>believe in his Name,</ns0:hi> whether <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Gentiles from their Sins</ns0:hi>: Hereby the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> hints the <ns0:hi>mistake</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> in thinking the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> should be a <ns0:hi>Temporal Saviour,</ns0:hi> who should save the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> from their Enemies, minding them, that he was to save them not from their Bodily but Spiritual Enemies, <ns0:hi>from their Sins</ns0:hi>: The Guilt of them, and the Power of them, and from the eternal Danger of them, and he alone should do it; <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 4.12. <ns0:hi>There is no other Name under Heaven given amongst men, neither is there Salvation in any</ns0:hi> other.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22. Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken of the Lord by the Prophet saying.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 Behold a Virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a Son, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>his <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> shall be called.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> they shall call his name Immanuel, which being interpreted, is God with us.<ns0:note place="bottom">By these great Acts of Divine Providence, that which was spoken, and Prophesied of by <ns0:hi>Isaiah, ch.</ns0:hi> 7.14. speaking by Inspiration from God, <ns0:hi>was fulfilled</ns0:hi>: Tho things are said in the <ns0:hi>Evangelists,</ns0:hi> to be fulfilled when the <ns0:hi>Types</ns0:hi> have had their ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complishment in the <ns0:hi>Antitype,</ns0:hi> and when something cometh to pass much like, or bearing some Proportion to something which before happened in the World (as I shall shew hereafter) yet I take the Sense of <ns0:hi>being fulfilled,</ns0:hi> here to be <ns0:hi>literally ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />filled</ns0:hi>; believing so much of that Prophecy as is here quoted, did literally concern Christ, and none but him. But we must take heed of interpreting the Particle <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> as signifying the end of <ns0:hi>Gods Action</ns0:hi> in this great work of Providence; for the <ns0:hi>End</ns0:hi> for which God sent his Son into the World, was before expressed, <ns0:hi>to save his People from their sins,</ns0:hi> not to fulfil a Prophecy. <ns0:hi>That</ns0:hi> here only signifies the consequent of that Act of divine Providence, and the Sense is but only this: <ns0:hi>By all this which was done, was fulfilled that which was spoken of the Lord by the Prophet,</ns0:hi> &c. But the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> so much Clamou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring against the Application of that Text, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 7.14. to Christ; and some learned Interpreters thinking the <ns0:hi>fulfilling</ns0:hi> mentioned to be no more then the fulfilling of a <ns0:hi>Type</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Antitype,</ns0:hi> it will be necessary that we make it appear that it was literally fulfilled. To which I know of but two Prejudices. 1. <ns0:hi>That it could be no relief to Ahaz, nor to the Iews</ns0:hi> against their Sense <ns0:hi>and Fear of their present Danger,</ns0:hi> to tell them that Christ <ns0:hi>should be born of a Virgin eight hundred years after.</ns0:hi> 2. That whereas <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. it is added. <ns0:hi>Before the Child shall know to refuse the Evil, and chuse the Good, the Land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her Kings.</ns0:hi> Supposing those two Kings, to be <ns0:hi>Pekah King of Israel,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rezin King</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> who were at that time joyned in a Siege against <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem,</ns0:hi> or at least preparing for it, and the Child mentioned <ns0:hi>v</ns0:hi> 16. to be the <ns0:hi>Son of a Virgin promised, v.</ns0:hi> 14. it could be no relief to <ns0:hi>Ahaz,</ns0:hi> nor any great News for the <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> to have told <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> that they should both leave the Country before eight hundred years were Elapsed. Let us therefore first consider the History to which that Prophecy related, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 7.1. we are told that in the time of <ns0:hi>Ahaz, Rezin</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>King of Syria</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pekah</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Remaliah</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>King of Israel went up towards Ierusalem to War against it, v.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>And it was told the House of David</ns0:hi> (that is <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi>) saying, <ns0:hi>Syria is Confederate with Ephraim; and his Heart was moved, and the Heart of his People, as the Trees of the Wood are moved with the W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nd.</ns0:hi> The expedient which <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> thought upon in this Distress, was to get <ns0:hi>Tiglah Peleser, the King of Assyria,</ns0:hi> to joyn with, and help him (which he afterward did) hiring him with <ns0:hi>the Silver and Gold found in the House of the Lord, and in the Trea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sures of the Kings House,</ns0:hi> as we find 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 1.6, 7. This Conjunction with <ns0:hi>Idolaters,</ns0:hi> was what the Lord had forbidden, and had often declared his abhorrence of. To prevent it, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. he sends his Prophet <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> to him, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 7.3. <ns0:hi>Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy Son at the end of the upper Pool in the High-way of the Fullers Field. And say unto him. Fear not, neither be Faint-hearted,</ns0:hi> &c. In short, he assureth him in the Name of the Lord, That the <ns0:hi>Counsel of</ns0:hi> these two Kings <ns0:hi>should not stand, nor come to pass, v.</ns0:hi> 7. that within threescore, and five years <ns0:hi>Israel should not be a People,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> knew not how to believe this. <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> offereth him from God to ask a <ns0:hi>Sign</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>Confirmation</ns0:hi> of his word, either <ns0:hi>in the heighth, or in the depth. Ahaz</ns0:hi> refuseth it under pretence that he would not <ns0:hi>Tempt the Lord,</ns0:hi> as if it had been a tempting God to have asked a Sign at his Command, at this the Lord was angry as appeareth by the Prophets reply, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 13. And he said, <ns0:hi>Hear ye now</ns0:hi> you House of <ns0:hi>David, is it a small thing for you to weary Men, but will you weary my God also?</ns0:hi> Then he goeth on. <ns0:hi>Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a Sign. Behold a Virgin,</ns0:hi> &c. There was nothing more ordinary in the <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> then to Comfort the People of God amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in their Distresses, with the <ns0:hi>Promise</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> this we find they often did with reference to the Captivity of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> and in other Causes of Distress and Trouble. And cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainly that is the design of the Prophet here, in these words: <ns0:hi>Behold a Virgin shall conceive, and bear a Son and shall call his Name Immanuel. Ahaz</ns0:hi> had refused to believe the <ns0:hi>Promise,</ns0:hi> God gave him, to defeat the <ns0:hi>Counsel</ns0:hi> of these two Kings, he had refused to ask a Sign, for the <ns0:hi>Confirmation</ns0:hi> of Gods word. Well (saith the Prophet) God<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> shall give you that fear him a Sign, he shall in his own time send you the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> whose name shall be called <ns0:hi>Immanuel,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>he shall be born of a Vir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gin.</ns0:hi> Nor yet doth he leave <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> and his people Comfortless, as to their present Distress, for saith he <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. <ns0:hi>Before the Child shall know to refuse the Evil, and to chuse the Good, the Land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her Kings.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> which I think were better translated: <ns0:hi>This Child,</ns0:hi> then <ns0:hi>the Child,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> seems not to be a <ns0:hi>Relative</ns0:hi> (referring to the Child mentioned in <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14.) but a <ns0:hi>Demonstra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tive</ns0:hi> referring to the Son of <ns0:hi>Isaiah Shear-jashub,</ns0:hi> whom God <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. Commanded the Prophet going to meet <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> to carry with him, (who probably) was a very young Child saith the Prophet. Here is a little Child whom God hath Commanded me to bring with me, before this Child be much older, this Land which thou art so much afraid of, shall be quitted of both those <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> who have now some Possession of it, for at this time, 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 16.6. <ns0:hi>Rezin</ns0:hi> had taken <ns0:hi>Elath</ns0:hi> a City of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi>; and doubtless he, and <ns0:hi>Pekah</ns0:hi> had taken di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vers places, for they were come up to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> it self. And indeed if this be not the Sense, it is very hard to conceive, to what purpose God Commanded <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> to take <ns0:hi>Shear-jashub</ns0:hi> with him. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 7.3. When he went upon this Errand. So that <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. remains as a <ns0:hi>Prophecy</ns0:hi> respecting the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> only, and given not for any relief of unbelieving <ns0:hi>Ahas</ns0:hi> as to his pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent Distress, but for some relief to Gods People among the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> with reference to their Posterity: This will appear a much more probable Sense than theirs, who think that <ns0:hi>Maher<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shalal-hashbaz</ns0:hi> is the Son mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. whom we read of, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 8.3. who was born to <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Prophetess,</ns0:hi> who some think was at this time a <ns0:hi>Virgin,</ns0:hi> and was a Type of Christ, for the Scripture doth not tell us whether that <ns0:hi>Prophetess</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Virgin,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Widow,</ns0:hi> neither was it any great wonder, that a <ns0:hi>Virgin</ns0:hi> being married should conceive, and bear a Son. Nor had this been any relief to <ns0:hi>Ahaz,</ns0:hi> as to his present Distress, for this Virgin (if she were such) was yet to be married, to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive and bear a Son, so that according to that Notion, we must allow three or four years, before <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> could have ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pected relief. This is further advantaged by that passage, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 8.18. <ns0:hi>Behold I and the Children which the Lord hath given me are for Signs.</ns0:hi> Not the Child but <ns0:hi>the Children. Shear-jashub,</ns0:hi> was for a Sign of Gods deliverance of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> from those two Kings, <ns0:hi>Maher-Shalal-hashbaz,</ns0:hi> was for a Sign of the Destruction of the <ns0:hi>Israelites, within five years,</ns0:hi> and also of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> which fell out afterward thus, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mains a litteral <ns0:hi>Prophecy</ns0:hi> of Christ. For the Jewish interpre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation of it, concerning <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> (born fifteen years after) it is too ridiculous to be mentioned.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:219" />24 Then Joseph being raised from sleep, did as the Angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And knew her not, until she had brought forth her first born Son. And he called his name Jesus.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Will of God (as we heard) was revealed to <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> in a Dream. It is God that giveth a Power to sleep, and a Pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er to <ns0:hi>awake</ns0:hi>: Therefore it is said, <ns0:hi>being raised from sleep,</ns0:hi> he shewed both his <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Obedience,</ns0:hi> his Faith in the <ns0:hi>Divine Revelation,</ns0:hi> a certainty of which he had doubtless by some extraordinary divine Impression and his Obedience to the di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Precept: <ns0:hi>He took unto him his Wife,</ns0:hi> that is, he took her unto his House (for betrothed Virgins, used to abide at their own Friends Houses, till the Consummation of the Marriage) and owning her as his Wife, yet not fully using her as such, for the Text saith <ns0:hi>he knew her not</ns0:hi> (a modest Phrase used from the beginning of the World, as appears from <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 4.1. to express the Conjugal Act) <ns0:hi>till she had brought forth her first born Son.</ns0:hi> Some make a great stir in determining, <ns0:hi>whether he knew her afterwards, yea or no</ns0:hi>: Some of the Ancients were stiff in their Opinion, that he did not, so are the <ns0:hi>Popish Writers,</ns0:hi> and many <ns0:hi>Protestant Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preters.</ns0:hi> Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> I think determines best, That none will move such a Question, but such as are <ns0:hi>unwarrantably curious,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>contend for either part,</ns0:hi> but such as are <ns0:hi>unrea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sonably Quarrelsome.</ns0:hi> For as on the one side, none can con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clude that she had more Children from the Word <ns0:hi>until,</ns0:hi> fur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther than, they can conclude from <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 110.1. That <ns0:hi>Christ shall not for ever sit at his Fathers right hand</ns0:hi> (the word <ns0:hi>Vn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />til</ns0:hi> being a Particle only exclusive of a preceeding time, not affirming the thing in future time. Nor doth the term <ns0:hi>First born</ns0:hi> conclude any <ns0:hi>born afterward:</ns0:hi> So on the other side, there are no cogent Arguments, to prove that <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> had no more Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren by <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> we read of the <ns0:hi>Brother of our Lord Galath.</ns0:hi> 1.19. and of his <ns0:hi>Mother,</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Brethren, Math.</ns0:hi> 12.47. and tho it be true, <ns0:hi>Brethren</ns0:hi> may signifie <ns0:hi>Kinsmen</ns0:hi> according to the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> dialect, yet that it doth so in these Texts cannot be prov'd. The Holy Ghost had made use of the <ns0:hi>Virgin</ns0:hi> for the Production of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> why after this, her Womb should be shut up, and <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> take her home to be his Wife, and not use her as such, I cannot tell, nor yet, what reproach it could be to <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> or to our Saviour, Marriage being Go<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Ordinance, and the <ns0:hi>undefiled Bed Honourable,</ns0:hi> and those who think our Saviour would have been dishonoured in any others lying in the same Bed, after him, seem to forget how much he humbled himself, in lying in that Bed first, and then <ns0:hi>in a Stable,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Manger</ns0:hi>; we know he knew her not till Christ was born, whether he did afterward or no, we are willingly ignorant because God hath not told us. <ns0:hi>And he call<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed his</ns0:hi> name <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi>: This is added to declare his Obedience to the Command received by the Angel. We shall meet with more Circumstances relating to the Birth of Christ, when we come to the two <ns0:hi>first Chapters</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Luke.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
